Lost bag, not so great customer service. My trip started with a delayed flight - which to be fair, the weather was not great. This caused me to miss my connection. I couldn’t get on the app to rebook - the app kept spinning. When I asked for help at the Houston airport - terminal E on June 15th- I was met with less than enthusiastic help by multiple United employees I approached. I ended up stuck from 10am to 7:50pm at the Houston airport and saw on the app that my bag somehow ended up on a
Flight to San Francisco. I kept asking for help and no one could give me answers. They told me I would need to speak to baggage which was outside the terminals. The worst interaction I had was with a United representative who actually put her hand up in my face and told me she, “didn’t have time for me.” I had barely got out, “May I ask you a quick question” when this happened. I ended up going into the lounge and crying because I was supposed to be meeting my friend who has cancer in Vancouver to leave on a cruise the next day and it seemed things were going south and no one could tell me what was going on with my bag. The lounge gave me a number to call and the lady in the lounge (I think her name was Tina) was trying to help and said my flight would arrive 2 hours before me in Vancouver from what she could see on the screen. I got to Vancouver. No bag. They had sent it back to Houston. So I had nothing to get on an Alaskan cruise but the clothes on my back. I had arrived close to midnight because of the delay and had to board the ship the next day so the next day was a rush of trying to get somewhere where I could pick up stuff because I had little hope they would get me my bag at the next port but no absolute assurance. The first couple days of my one week cruise was spent at customer service trying to locate my bag and making sure everyone was communicating. The first day we found out this time my bag had somehow ended up in Seattle. When we got to Juno my bag finally arrived but I had to Uber to the airport to pick it up and get it on the ship. These trips are not cheap and I lost a lot of time which wasn’t ideal. I’ve been assured that I will be refunded for the stuff I had to buy and that is giving me some anxiety. Hoping that won’t be a fight or hassle on top of what was already a very stressful experience.

Updates are belligerent. The purveyors of this app must think we’ve got nothing else to do like we have no other apps to keep track of. 
Rather than do the work upfront to develop a smart fully functional and intuitive application that customers want, and serve their needs efficiently with minimal updates and changes, so that we can focus on our lives… the stewards of this online tool are constantly changing it like it’s a clothing style that they want to keep fresh. 

Very rarely is anything improved, it’s just rearranged so that you have to learn new ways to accomplish the same functions

The simple offline capabilities that we need, like all pertinent Flight information in one place are ignored. Consistency, and intuitiveness are sacrificed for appearance, and change for the sake of I don’t know what personal edification, bragging rights at the software convention? Who knows. 
And efficient functionality is neglected to prioritize marketing Objectives and personal preferences of the people fielding the application.

The worst part is the updates. They are insanely intrusive, and frequent. Worse, They are too lazy to make them backward-compatible, so you find yourself in a place with poor or no connectivity, and open the app to find information only to get a message, “this app is out of date”. It won’t even give you the information you’ve saved, it breaks your phone for Flight support. I can’t imagine a manager accepting this product when IT brings it.
